title: Diffusion: why a smell spreads across a room
examples: Why can I smell cooking from another room?
Why is diffusion faster when it is hot?

explain.say: Imagine someone opens a box of hot samosas at the far end of the room. A moment later, you can smell them! How did the smell reach your nose? Look at the board and watch two kinds of particles.

draw.text: Diffusion: why a smell spreads across a room

explain.say: See how at first the coloured particles are all bunched on one side? That is a high concentration, which means lots of particles crowded in one place. Where do you think they will go next?

Yes, they spread out! The particles bump about at random and drift from where there are many to where there are few, until they are evenly mixed. This spreading is called diffusion. Can you think of a smell that reaches you before you see its source?

Now look at the reasons on the board. When it is warm, particles have more energy and move faster, so they spread sooner. That is why hot masala chai smells stronger than cold chai. Does that match what you have noticed?

draw.answer: Hot particles move faster, so they spread out sooner

explain.say: Brilliant! Diffusion happens in gases and in liquids. Colour drifting out of a tea bag is diffusion too, just slower, because liquid particles are closer together. Wow: your lungs pass oxygen into your blood by diffusion, with every breath you take.

faq.a: Diffusion is particles spreading out from where there are lots of them to where there are fewer, because they move about at random. It goes on until they are evenly mixed.

faq.q: Why does diffusion go faster when it is hot?
faq.a: Heat gives particles more energy, so they move faster and spread out sooner. That is why hot food smells stronger than cold food.

faq.q: Why is diffusion slower in a liquid than in a gas?
faq.a: Liquid particles are close together and keep bumping into each other, so they cannot travel far before changing direction. Gas particles have big gaps and move faster.
asks: Why does ink spread slowly in water?

faq.a: Hardly at all. Particles in a solid are fixed in place and only vibrate, so they cannot wander off. Diffusion happens mainly in liquids and gases.

faq.q: Where does diffusion happen in the body?
faq.a: In your lungs, oxygen diffuses from the air into your blood, and carbon dioxide diffuses out. Digested food also diffuses from your gut into your blood.
asks: How does oxygen get into the blood?

facts: Diffusion is the net movement of particles from a region of higher concentration to a region of lower concentration.
Diffusion is faster at higher temperatures because the particles move faster.
